inventory.visualPurpose: The two vector figures — the progression strip (215) and the grade-vs-stage art (216)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: VECTOR LINE ART (pdfimages: ZERO raster images on either page). p237: the five-panel progression strip — normal epithelium with basal-to-apical polarity over an intact basement membrane with a stromal vessel → disorganized pleomorphic cells still above the membrane → atypical cells filling the entire epithelial thickness with the membrane intact → cells breaching the membrane into the stroma → cells entering the vessel lumen for distant spread; labels print once over panel 1 ('Epithelial cell layer / Basement membrane / Blood or lymphatic vessel') but interleave 3× in the text layer with fused fragments. p238: low/high-grade tissue circles, T with a primary-tumor glyph, N with two lymph-node drawings, M with a blood-or-lymphatic-vessel drawing and 'Spread to other organs and tissues' — labels duplicated 2× with fused fragments.

notes: Both pages' text blocks (the definition, the five stations, the naming rules, the malformation pair, the 9-row table, the grade/stage columns) are adapted as the registry visual and carried verbatim in the note's tables. The TWO figures are pure vector line art (zero rasters) — redrawn as ORIGINAL KYP glyphs (the P2/P3 convention): the five-station progression strip with its three labels and the grade-vs-stage art with its T/N/M glyphs. Table quirks preserved and documented: 'Mesenchyme' is a row-group label spanning Blood cells through Fat; the Blood cells BENIGN cell prints empty (leukemia/lymphoma malignant-only); melanoma wears no carcinoma/sarcoma suffix. No margin mnemonics exist on either page; nothing reproduced. STAGING — registration + content/ flip belong to the main session.
